agents.final: I published one event, EV-0001: scoop 7 (LH-07) is down at 1310-04 (TP-1310-04) with a hydraulic pressure loss. The operator says it can't move on its own. Maintenance guesses a hydraulic pump and at least 4 hours, but that is a guess made before inspection, so I recorded it with lower reliability. The supervisor's note that 1310-04 is the shift's high-grade stope, and the shift boss's search for a replacement scoop, are in the payload. Both mentions resolved. I skipped the routine chatter.

I published two CMMS events for LH-07, the only equipment with an open failure (EV-0001). Both resolved to LH-07 with no unresolved mentions.

- **EV-0002, maintenance record:** LH-07 has three closed corrective hydraulic work orders, all flagged chronic. They are OT-2041, OT-2068 (hydraulic pump repair, 5.0 h) and OT-2095, totalling 11.0 repair hours.
- **EV-0003, maintenance plan:** OT-2110, the 500 h hydraulic system inspection, is overdue and high priority. It was scheduled for 2026-06-26.

I submitted assessment PR-0001 for LH-07, the only open equipment failure. It estimates a repair of 4 to 7 hours, most likely 5, with the scoop back at about 14:30 on the shift clock. The 4-hour low case would put it back at 13:30 and the 7-hour high case at 16:30. Confidence is 0.6.

- **Cause:** The likely cause is the hydraulic pump, but that is only the crew's guess by sound.
- **Basis for 5 hours:** The last pump repair on this scoop (OT-2068) took 5.0 hours, and the crew said "minimum four hours." It also has three chronic hydraulic repairs in about five weeks and an overdue hydraulic inspection (OT-2110).
- **Not yet known:** Someone needs to get the inspection result from the crew at 1310-04. They should also check whether a spare pump is in stock and whether the repair can be done on site, since the scoop can't move under its own power.

I submitted proposal PR-0002 for approval: move LH-11 from TP-1250-02 to TP-1310-04 to cover the failed LH-07, starting by 09:35. It nets about 32.4 oz protected, and my confidence is 0.7 because the repair time is unconfirmed.

- **Do nothing:** loses 225 t and 60.8 oz at TP-1310-04.
- **Wait for repair:** the likely repair finishes at 14:30, which loses 150 t and 40.5 oz.
- **Move LH-11:** TP-1250-02 is the lowest-grade loading-only stope, at 4.1 g/t. The ramp move to 1310 takes 1 h. It protects 192.5 t and 52.0 oz at TP-1310-04 and loses 148.3 t and 19.5 oz at TP-1250-02. Total at risk drops to 180.8 t and 28.3 oz.
- **Move LH-10 instead:** the same-level move is faster, but the net is only 24.5 oz because the donor stope grades 6.0 g/t.

I kept LH-11 at 1310-04 until 17:00. Sending it back after LH-07 is repaired could recover some of the 19.5 oz, but I did not count that.

The repair time is still a crew guess by sound (4–7 h). Someone should check the inspection result, spare pump availability and whether the ramp to 1310 is clear.
